heroHeadline: Israel Intercepts Flotilla 600 Nautical Miles from Gaza; Turkey Calls It 'Piracy' — Save the Children: Settler Violence Displaces 10x More Palestinian Children in 2026
heroSubtitle: Israeli naval forces intercepted the Global Sumud Flotilla on April 29–30 in international waters near Crete — 600 nautical miles from Gaza — seizing 22 of 58 vessels and detaining approximately 175 activists. Turkey condemned it as 'an act of piracy'; Italy condemned the 'unlawful' seizure. A six-month humanitarian scorecard published April 2026 found the ceasefire 'is failing,' with aid at 25% of agreed levels and 92% of Gaza's housing destroyed. Save the Children reported settler violence has displaced 685 Palestinian children in the first three months of 2026 — ten times the previous average — with 170 Palestinians injured by settlers in March 2026 alone, the highest monthly count since 2006.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Euronews, Yesh Din, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
